newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures rise late, end light trade mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures rise late, end light trade mixed.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished mixed after a late runup in light, holiday-like conditions.

The long end popped up during the final hour, with the short end trailing behind, after a Federal Reserve source was quoted in a Reuters story as saying the Fed is close to adopting core consumer price index as the basis for monetary policy.
The story sparked a rise in trading already subdued by a holiday in Japan overnight and the Jewish Yom Kippur holiday.
"It was really thin in here," said a Eurodollar broker, who said estimated volume on price boards was about 125,000.

"There were no locals in here, no sellers," said a broker in T-bond futures, adding that the December futures advanced on moderate buying from a couple of dealers but that no stops were triggered on the advance.
Some traders also wondered exactly how to interpret the source's remarks in terms of whether that means the Fed has more work to do against inflation.
Core CPI currently is rising at a 2.6-percent annual rate.
"Is 2.6 percent core high or low now?" asked the Eurodollar broker.
Traders waited to see whether the Federal Open Market Committee raises rates at its meeting on Tuesday, with many looking for a quarter-point increase and others foreseeing no action.
December T-bonds on the rise cleared Friday's low at 107-21/32 after holding the two-week low early at 107-14/32.
Dec T-bonds rose 11/32 to 108-03/32, bills lost one bp to 94.62, Eurodollars ended flat at 94.06, muni-bonds rose 15/32 to 113-03/32, and T-notes gained 6.32 to 106-17/32.
